lines.trans: Hello, is there nobody besides the head chef to bring a bottle?
You will be very surprised, but I am worried about you.
Did you really come to treat me yourself today?
Yes, I came to you with hot soup.
After all, you have not eaten properly for four days already.
I cooked your favorite onion soup for you.
And brought a glass of good wine for your health.
Since you are so caring, let us drink to my health.
Or did you secretly slip something into my wine?
So that I fall asleep and you take me to the mental clinic?

examples.text: Денег мне хватает или ещё у официантов просить.
examples.trans: Whether I have enough money or need to ask the waiters too.

examples.text: Или ты мне в вино что-то тайком подсыпал?
examples.trans: Or did you secretly slip something into my wine?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А ты чего совсем не улыбаешься?
examples.trans: And why are you not smiling at all?

examples.text: Вы обе с этой минуты уволены!
examples.trans: You are both fired as of this minute!

examples.text: Виктор, она уволила семь горничных за три дня.
examples.trans: Viktor, she fired seven maids in three days.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'something; somehow', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Слушай, а у вас с Денисом что-то есть?
examples.trans: Listen, is there something going on between you and Denis?

examples.text: Или ты мне в вино что-то тайком подсыпал?
examples.trans: Or did you secretly slip something into my wine?

examples.text: Скажи честно, для тебя это что-то значит?
examples.trans: Tell me honestly, does this mean something to you?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'secretly', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Или ты мне в вино что-то тайком подсыпал?
examples.trans: Or did you secretly slip something into my wine?

examples.text: Костя сказал это совершенно тайком и спокойно.
examples.trans: Kostya said this quite secretly and calmly.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'сыпать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'slipped / poured in'.

examples.text: Или ты мне в вино что-то тайком подсыпал?
examples.trans: Or did you secretly slip something into my wine?

examples.text: Я лекарство не в вино, а в суп подсыпал!
examples.trans: I slipped the medicine not into the wine, but into the soup!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'so that, in order to', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Слушай, а у вас с Денисом что-то есть?
examples.trans: Listen, is there something going on between you and Denis?

examples.text: Что, теперь скажешь маме, чтобы меня уволили?
examples.trans: What, now you will tell your mom to fire me?

examples.text: И что ты ей на это ответила?
examples.trans: And what did you answer her to that?

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'снуть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to fall asleep', paired with 'засыпать'.

examples.text: Чтобы я уснула, а ты меня в психушку увёз?
examples.trans: So that I fall asleep and you take me to the mental clinic?

examples.text: Он быстро уснёт после укола.
examples.trans: He will fall asleep quickly after the injection.

examples.text: Ребёнок крепко уснул.
examples.trans: The child fell fast asleep.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Скажи, чего ты так радостно улыбаешься?
examples.trans: Tell me, why are you smiling so cheerfully?

examples.text: А ты чего совсем не улыбаешься?
examples.trans: And why are you not smiling at all?

examples.text: Виктор, она уволила семь горничных за три дня.
examples.trans: Viktor, she fired seven maids in three days.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'mental clinic' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: За мои деньги хочешь меня в психушку отправить?
examples.trans: For my own money you want to send me to a mental clinic?

examples.text: Чтобы я уснула, а ты меня в психушку увёз?
examples.trans: So that I fall asleep and you take me to the mental clinic?

увезти.gloss: to take away (by vehicle), drive away

meanings.en: to take away, drive someone/something away
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'везти'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to take away (by vehicle), drive away', paired with 'увозить'.

examples.text: Его нужно куда-то увезти.
examples.trans: We need to take him away somewhere.

examples.text: Их увезли на дачу.
examples.trans: They were driven out to the dacha.

examples.text: Его нужно куда-то увезти, понимаете?
examples.trans: We need to take him away somewhere, do you understand?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on, well', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вы обе с этой минуты уволены!
examples.trans: You are both fired as of this minute!

examples.text: Элеонора Андреевна, вам нужно сменить обстановку.
examples.trans: Eleonora Andreevna, you need a change of scenery.

examples.text: Безусловно, вам нужен полный покой и отдых.
examples.trans: Without a doubt, you need complete peace and rest.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Слушай, а у вас с Денисом что-то есть?
examples.trans: Listen, is there something going on between you and Denis?

examples.text: Что, теперь скажешь маме, чтобы меня уволили?
examples.trans: What, now you will tell your mom to fire me?

examples.text: И что ты ей на это ответила?
examples.trans: And what did you answer her to that?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'speak', paired with 'сказать'.

examples.text: Поговори с ней, ведь наш бизнес страдает.
examples.trans: Talk to her, because our business is suffering.

examples.text: Ну что ты говоришь, давай выпьем за тебя.
examples.trans: What are you saying, let us drink to you.

examples.text: Слушай, ты ведь уже поговорила со Светой?
examples.trans: Listen, you already talked with Sveta, right?

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'medicine' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я лекарство не в вино, а в суп подсыпал!
examples.trans: I slipped the medicine not into the wine, but into the soup!

examples.text: Может быть, лекарства какие-то?
examples.trans: Maybe some medicine?

examples.text: Врач выписал новое лекарство.
examples.trans: The doctor prescribed a new medicine.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'doctor' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Миша, срочно вызывай её личного врача.
examples.trans: Misha, urgently call her personal doctor.

examples.text: Быстро вызывай сюда врача!
examples.trans: Quickly call the doctor here!

examples.text: Врачи могут заходить, всё готово.
examples.trans: The doctors can come in, everything is ready.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.text: А ты не могла бы мне немного помочь?
examples.trans: Could you help me a little bit?

examples.text: Просто ей нужно немного помочь с правильным выбором.
examples.trans: She just needs a little help with the right choice.

examples.text: Сегодня не могу.
examples.trans: I can't today.

заходить.gloss: to come in, to drop in

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to come in, to drop in', paired with 'зайти'.

examples.text: Врачи могут заходить, всё готово.
examples.trans: The doctors can come in, everything is ready.

examples.text: Заходите, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Please come in.

examples.text: Заходи, Федя. Садись на стул.
examples.trans: Come in, Fedya. Sit down on the chair.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Решайтесь быстрее, мне же надо всё посчитать.
examples.trans: Decide faster, I need to count everything up.

examples.text: Врачи могут заходить, всё готово.
examples.trans: The doctors can come in, everything is ready.

examples.text: Катя, скажи, у тебя всё в порядке?
examples.trans: Katya, tell me, is everything alright with you?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('ready').

examples.text: Я тебе твой любимый луковый суп приготовил.
examples.trans: I cooked your favorite onion soup for you.

examples.text: Врачи могут заходить, всё готово.
examples.trans: The doctors can come in, everything is ready.

examples.text: Сразу готовим все ваши документы на проверку.
examples.trans: Immediately prepare all your documents for inspection.
